subject: How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?

messages.author: 281bf392d852a6b2
messages.subject: How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?
parts: I have case and control samples in two separate methlyRaw object. I used read.bismark to import SAM files. Is it possible to merge those two methylRaw objects into single methylRaw object?

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?
parts: you can make a new methylRawList object, that can contain multiple methylRaw objects? is that what you are asking? It doesn't generally makes sense to combine two methylRaw objects in a new methylRaw object

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?
parts:
Hi,

I have almost 90 Bismark aligned SAM files and each SAM file is more than 15GB in size. I am running in the machine having 96GB of RAM and 24 processor cores. Still i am unable to import all 90 SAM files using read.bismark. I get outof memory eroor. eve if it completes It seems it will take weeks to complete. I was wondering If I could import those SAM files into methylRaw object separately and merge them later.
On Monday, August 17, 2015 at 12:17:29 AM UTC+3, Altuna Akalin wrote:

you can make a new methylRawList object, that can contain multiple methylRaw objects? is that what you are asking? It doesn't generally makes sense to combine two methylRaw objects in a new methylRaw object

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?
parts:
We are working on a solution that will consume less memory but I dont have an eta on that.

But, Yes you can do what you suggested you need to create a new methylRaw object after you rbind the dataframe parts of them. Alternatively, if you are good with programming you can help us develop the first thing I mentioned.

Best
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?
parts:
Hi Altuna,

Thank you the reply. I would be happy to contribute, but I have very busy schedule and could not promise anything at this moment. I managed to deal with this situation in another way. I executed read.bismark() on every single SAM file in parallel in compute nodes and saved methylation call files. Later I imported methylation call files using read() function. It was rather fast and took only 1.5 days to create methylation call files for all samples.

Now I am having another problem. When I filter methylation level based on coverage(=10), I got the following error. When I filtered by coverage=50, I did not get the error.


> filtered.meth.raw <- filterByCoverage(meth.raw, lo.count = 10,lo.perc = NULL,
+ hi.count = NULL, hi.perc = 99.9)
> meth.bases <- unite(filtered.meth.raw, destrand = TRUE)

If that's ok, try including `j` and dropping `by` (by-without-by) so that j runs for each group to avoid the large allocation. If you are sure you wish to proceed, rerun with allow.cartesian=TRUE. messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I merge two or more methylRaw objects?
parts:
this is probably due to duplicate coordinates in the file not directly related to the coverage cutoff. also you are not using the latest version of methylKit, you should upgrade and see if the error persists.

best,
Altuna
